lines.text: Two knocks. One hummed B-flat, slightly flat. The door with no handle swings open onto stairs that smell of brass polish and old fish.
At the bottom is a cellar full of instruments, mismatched chairs and a small stage lit by one stubborn bulb.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Well, look who found the stairs. And you brought half the harbor's attention with you.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: Sorry. Um. I tried to keep it down. Mostly.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Don't apologize down here, kid. Down here, loud is polite. I'm Ruby. Most folks call me Ma Ruby, and the rest owe me money.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: I'm Pip. I play the... well. You heard.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Half of Port Murmur heard. You walked through a square full of Quiet Squad with a crowd humming around you. That's the point.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [I did do that. I would like to faint about it later.]

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: The Brass Cellar has been open thirty years. Since the Silence Act, nearly every musician in town has packed up or gone quiet.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Old Jonas sold his accordion yesterday. Said the fines cost more than the music was worth.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: It is. So we're putting on a concert. A secret one, right here, with every player still brave enough to show up.

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: First, people need to know where and when. Ever put up posters, kid? At night? With the Squad watching?

lines.speaker: ruby
lines.text: Terribly. Wear dark socks, bring a pot of glue, and don't play a single note.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.text: [No trumpet. In the dark. With glue. Fantastic.]
